items.title: Russian Forces Kill Last Resident of Kherson Village Tiahynka
items.description: Russian forces have killed the last remaining resident of the frontline village of Tiahynka in Ukraine’s Kherson region, with the elderly man’s remains discovered during an Oct. 30 localized truce. The man had returned home despite receiving a written death threat from Russian soldiers, Tiahynka Village Military Admini…

items.title: Gaza strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff Israel links to Hamas
items.description: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) voiced outrage on Saturday after an Israeli strike killed two staff members at a clinic in Gaza, while the Israeli military said the pair were Hamas "terrorists". The Friday night strike in Gaza City drew swift condemnation from the head of the UN's World Health Organization and came despi…

items.title: Iran points to Europe’s war role after Italians killed in Kuwait strike
items.description: Italy and Kuwait say an Iranian drone was involved, but Tehran says the US and Israel may be looking to escalate war.

items.title: Two Médecins Sans Frontières staff killed by Israeli strike in Gaza, charity says
items.description: MSF and head of WHO denounce attack on Gaza City clinic as Israel claims security guards were members of HamasIsraeli forces have bombed a clinic run by Médecins Sans Frontières in Gaza City, killing two of its staff members, the organisation has said.MSF said Israel had directly struck the clinic, despite the fact tha…

items.title: As Spain votes, what could change for Europe?
items.description: Spain votes on Sunday. A loss for Pedro Sanchez and a shift to the right in Madrid could affect how one of the EU's largest countries approaches migration, defense and the war in Gaza.

items.title: Two staff killed in Israeli strike on Gaza medical clinic, MSF says
items.description: The Israeli military says it targeted "Hamas terrorists" in the strike which has been condemned by the World Health Organization.

items.title: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, veteran rebel leader Thomas Lubanga launches a new offensive
items.description: In 2012, Lubanga became the first person convicted by the International Criminal Court for recruiting child soldiers in 2002 and 2003. Now exiled in Uganda, he is heading an insurgent group that has been advancing toward Bunia since mid-November.

items.title: 16 Days of Activism: UNHCR warns over deep funding cuts to vital protection work
items.description: Serious funding cuts are severely weakening protection for refugee and stateless women and girls and others at risk of gender-based violence (GBV), like Mariam, who survived a decade of captivity and rape at the hands of Boko Haram militia.

items.title: How the Iran war ripples unexpectedly out to rolling English farm country
items.description: Home to a military airfield, this rural community has seen repeated disruptions due to threats arising from conflict in the Middle East.

items.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
items.description: As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine Hold First Exchange of War Dead Since Rebooted Peace Talks
items.description: Russia returned 250 bodies to Ukraine and received 22 fallen Russian soldiers in exchange, officials in Moscow said.

items.title: 'We Became A Target': RFE/RL Reporter On Being Hunted By Russian Drones
items.description: RFE/RL war correspondent Maryan Kushnir describes how drone warfare has transformed Ukraine’s front line, the growing danger of Russian attacks on Kyiv, his own experience of surviving an attack, and the families searching for missing loved ones.
